dossier.name: Jason Calacanis
dossier.role: Founder and CEO of LAUNCH. He also runs the LAUNCH Accelerator, The Syndicate and Founder University, and is a fund manager.
dossier.thesis: He backs early-stage founders at pre-seed and seed, and writes a lot of small cheques across about 100 new companies a year. LAUNCH combines an accelerator, funds, a syndicate and a media platform (podcasts, events) to source deals and help founders.
dossier.stages: Pre-seed and seed, with follow-ons through The Syndicate
dossier.cheque: Figures vary by source and are not officially published. Third-party profiles put his personal angel cheques at about $25K–$100K. The LAUNCH Accelerator is commonly reported at $125K, and syndicate SPVs can reach $250K–$2M+. Confirm exact terms with LAUNCH directly.
looks_for: Founders who can state the problem and why they are the right team (third-party summary)

brief.headline: Jason Calacanis writes many small pre-seed and seed cheques and rewards fast, clear-speaking founders, which suits an early live-events app that can show real usage.
brief.angle: Pitch it as a simple problem with a sharp team behind it: a concert ticket is the start of a night out, and nobody owns the bars, merch and rides around it. Show you move fast with early usage or customer discovery, and say plainly that you are asking for a small cheque with a possible path to follow-on support through The Syndicate.

name_drop.line: Our customer data shows a strong taste overlap with Robinhood's audience, which suggests our fans are comfortable doing everything in one app.
name_drop.name: Robinhood

name_drop.line: Like Thumbtack, we connect people to local providers, except ours are bars, merch and rides, matched to a specific fanbase on a specific night.
name_drop.name: Thumbtack

name_drop.line: Our customers also overlap strongly with Calm's audience, which tells us they value an app that takes the stress out of a plan.
name_drop.name: Calm

deck: Open with one slide that states the problem and why your team is the right one to solve it, since he looks for founders who can say both clearly.
Show early customer discovery or usage up front, even if it is small, because he backs founders who execute fast.
Walk through one real concert night from ticket to pre-show bar, merch and ride, with the picks tailored to that fanbase.
Use Ticketmaster, Spotify and Uber as shorthand for ticketing, taste-based curation and rides, then show your own numbers rather than leaning on the names.
Close with a small, specific ask and what you will ship and learn with it, since he spreads small cheques across about 100 companies a year.

openers.line: You built This Week in Startups around founders explaining their business in plain terms, so I will try to do the same in two minutes.
openers.name: This Week in Startups

openers.line: I'm interested in how innovation actually spreads, and our app is a small case of it: ticketing already works, but the night around it was never connected.
openers.based_on: How Innovation Works: Serendipity, Energy and the Saving of Time
openers.name: How Innovation Works: Serendipity, Energy and the Saving of Time

openers.line: We lean on data to decide which bars and merch each fanbase gets, so I would love your read on where we should trust the numbers and where we should not.
openers.name: Data Skeptic

avoid: Do not pitch a big lead round or a late-stage story, since his focus is small cheques at pre-seed and seed.
Do not stay vague on the problem or the team, because he looks for founders who state both clearly.
Do not rely on big comparables or projections without any early usage or customer discovery to back them.
questions: Why are you the right team to build this, and what have you already shipped?
What early usage or customer discovery do you have, and what did it teach you?
Why would a fan use your app instead of just buying a ticket and sorting out the night themselves?
